newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Budget just first step for NZ govt, says Peters.
newsitem.headline: Budget just first step for NZ govt, says Peters.

text.p: Treasurer Winston Peters said on Friday that his June 26 budget would be just the first step in the coalition government's programme.
"It's an ambitious programme and we will need three years to put it fully in place," he said in a speech to Federated Farmers in New Plymouth.
He said the budget outline was contained within the coalition agreement signed by the National and New Zealand First parties in December.
"Next month's budget will again show that the coalition's programme is being adhered to."
To maintain a growth-friendly environment, Peters said that it was clear the government had to:
* maintain a conservative fiscal policy and predictable monetary policy so businesses did not have to second guess the government
* create a welfare system that encouraged more people to work
* ensure high quality education for all New Zealanders
* improve the efficiency of markets by reform of regulations and taxes
* encourage New Zealanders to save so they will benefit more from growth.
"The government has not forgotten the need to keep a tight rein on expenditure and keep repaying debt as fast as possible.
"What we want is a balance between spending, debt repayment and tax reductions that will allow us to meet all of our objectives," he said.

Peters said that when the government argued for a rethink on tax cuts over new spending, postponing the second round of cuts for a year, it had regard to the Reserve Bank to ensure economic objectives could be met.
"Therefore, this government will continue to run substantial fiscal surpluses to further reduce public debt and boost national savings," Peters said.
